clue.text: Time with teacher to pen question for game show

indicators.note: to pen something is to shut it inside, so one piece is enclosed by the others

parts.note: T is the standard abbreviation for time
to question someone is to ask
a schoolmaster is a teacher

explanation.surface: A teacher is drafted in to write quiz questions for a TV game show.
explanation.walkthrough: Time and teacher sit together and between them they hold the question.
explanation.definitionFit: Taskmaster is a British TV comedy panel show in which celebrities attempt odd tasks.

clue.text: Appeal sent upstairs, then very loud row

indicators.note: in a down clue, sending something upstairs means reading it from the bottom up

parts.note: it means sex appeal, as in having 'it'
fortissimo, the musical marking for very loud

explanation.surface: A plea is passed upstairs, and then comes a noisy argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' as sex appeal is a crossword favourite; reversed it sits in front of the musical marking.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiff is a minor quarrel, the same as a row.

clue.text: Person who won't play with anyone?

definitions.text: Person who won't play with anyone?

parts.words: Person who won't play with anyone?
parts.note: surface reading: an unsociable child who refuses to join in games
setter's reading: a musician who performs alone, without accompaniment

explanation.surface: A sulky loner refuses to join anyone else's games.
explanation.walkthrough: Play is musical playing, not children's games.
explanation.definitionFit: A soloist is a musician performing a solo part, playing by themselves.

clue.text: Glibness, possibly, that could have its pros and cons

definitions.text: that could have its pros and cons

parts.note: surface reading: a glib manner might be an advantage or a drawback
setter's reading: the letters of the word are a jumbled version of a word meaning a gift from heaven

explanation.surface: Being glib can be useful or harmful, depending on the occasion.
explanation.walkthrough: Glibness rearranged spells a word for a divine favour, so it is that word mixed up; the whole phrase then names something with good and bad sides.
explanation.definitionFit: A mixed blessing is something with both advantages and disadvantages, pros and cons.

clue.text: Second bed available without charge?

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for second
a cot is a small bed
free means not taken, available

explanation.surface: A spare bed is offered at no cost.
explanation.definitionFit: To get off scot-free is to escape without penalty or payment; charge works in both senses.

clue.text: Stop ignoring pair's affair

indicators.note: ignoring something leaves it out, so those letters are dropped

parts.note: to stop something happening is to prevent it
PR is the abbreviation for pair

explanation.surface: Someone is urged to stop overlooking a couple's romance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Affair' suggests romance, but here it simply means an occasion.
explanation.definitionFit: An affair can be any happening or occasion, which is an event.

clue.text: Breathe in sharply when doctor's brought round

indicators.note: bringing something round another surrounds it, wrapping one piece about the other

parts.note: a GP is a general practitioner, a family doctor
as can mean when, as in 'as he arrived'

explanation.surface: A patient gulps air as the doctor revives them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brought round' suggests reviving someone from a faint, but it tells the doctor to surround the other word.
explanation.definitionFit: To gasp is to draw breath suddenly, through shock or exertion.

clue.text: Is the compiler competent and friendly?

parts.note: the setter asking about themself: am I
able means capable, competent

explanation.surface: The setter wonders aloud whether they are skilled and likeable.
explanation.walkthrough: The compiler is the setter, so the question becomes 'am I able?' in the first person.
explanation.definitionFit: Amiable means good-natured and pleasant, which is friendly.

clue.text: Acting as plane perhaps coming for Spooner

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so the initial sounds of two words trade places

parts.note: the plane is a kind of tree, hence 'perhaps'; Spooner swaps its opening sound for a P
pending means about to happen, forthcoming; its opening P is swapped for a T

explanation.surface: Someone serves as an aircraft that is about to arrive, if Spooner says so.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the opening sounds of 'tree pending' and you get 'pree tending'. 'Plane' looks like an aircraft but is the tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Pretending means putting on an act, play-acting.

clue.text: Man with iron, 59

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
59 in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A man of iron is described by a bare number, like a convict.
explanation.walkthrough: Roman numerals: L is 50, IX is 9.
explanation.definitionFit: Felix is a male first name, so it stands for a man.

clue.text: Revolutionary musical about Post Office worker

indicators.note: a revolutionary thing turns over, so the whole string of pieces runs backwards

parts.note: Evita is the Lloyd Webber musical
re means about, concerning
PO is the abbreviation for Post Office

explanation.surface: A revolutionary-themed musical tells the story of a postal employee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' fits Evita's politics, but it reverses the whole run of pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: An operative is a worker, especially a factory hand or agent.

clue.text: Opinionated and horribly vague trite man

indicators.note: something done horribly is botched and disordered, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: the fodder letters, taken as written

explanation.surface: A man full of fixed views is also dreadfully woolly and clichéd.
explanation.definitionFit: An argumentative person is quarrelsome and pushes their views, much like someone opinionated.

clue.text: Never wearying of being a fat idle drunk

indicators.note: a drunk is unsteady and muddled, so the letters stagger into a new order

parts.note: the fodder letters, taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is never tired of being a lazy, overweight drinker.
explanation.walkthrough: The irony is that a fat idle drunk is the opposite of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Indefatigable means tireless, never growing weary.

clue.text: "Trader's mine," seaman reported

indicators.note: something reported is spoken about, so the words are taken by their sound

parts.note: a mine is a hole in the ground
a sailor is a seaman

explanation.surface: A sailor claims that a merchant belongs to him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trader's mine' reads as possession, but mine is the pit.
explanation.definitionFit: A wholesaler is a trader who sells goods in bulk to retailers.

clue.text: Spicy pork pie eaten by the Major, ultimately, and Basil Fawlty?

parts.note: spicy food is hot

indicators.note: what is eaten goes inside the eater, so one piece ends up enclosed
ultimately points to the end of each word, keeping only final letters

parts.note: last letters of the two words
rhyming slang: pork pie means lie

explanation.surface: A hot pork pie is eaten by the Major, a guest at Fawlty Towers.
explanation.walkthrough: Pork pie is Cockney rhyming slang for lie. Basil Fawlty runs the hotel in the British sitcom Fawlty Towers, where the Major is a resident.
explanation.definitionFit: Basil Fawlty is a hotel owner, an example of the answer, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Threaten troublemaker with death

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous troublemaker
death is one's end

explanation.surface: A troublemaker is threatened with being killed.
explanation.definitionFit: To impend is to loom or hang over menacingly, as a threat does.

clue.text: Dish that might be given to convict

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a hot oat cereal served in a bowl

definitions.text: that might be given to convict
definitions.meaning: second meaning: British slang for a prison sentence

explanation.walkthrough: Doing porridge is British slang for serving time in prison, also the title of a sitcom.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both an oatmeal breakfast and, in slang, a jail term handed to a criminal.

clue.text: Most weak metals melted

indicators.note: melted things lose their shape and can be recast, so the letters are reformed

parts.note: the fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: The feeblest metals are those that have melted.
explanation.definitionFit: Lamest is the superlative of lame, meaning feeblest or least convincing.

clue.text: Wicked: stupendously ace film!

indicators.note: stupendously suggests something wild and over the top, so the letters are thrown about

parts.note: the fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: A rave review: wicked, an amazingly brilliant movie!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wicked' reads as slang praise for the film, but the answer takes its old meaning of evil.
explanation.definitionFit: Malefic means causing harm or evil, a literary synonym of wicked.

clue.text: Drop blue act

parts.note: feeling blue is feeling down
a turn is a performer's act

explanation.surface: Someone is told to drop their smutty routine.
explanation.walkthrough: Blue here sounds like risqué comedy, but it means sad.
explanation.definitionFit: A downturn is a decline, a drop in activity or prices.

clue.text: Experimental and not given a hearing?

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a case or defendant not yet brought before a court

explanation.walkthrough: A hearing is a court session, so the second sense is legal.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both untested and not having been judged in court.

clue.text: Pompous fancy man flirts with poet

indicators.note: fancy implies elaborate invention, so the letters are dressed up in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A conceited dandy is flirting with a poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Self-important describes someone with an inflated sense of their own worth, which is pompous.

clue.text: Spread covering large dish

indicators.note: something covering another goes round it, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: pâté is a meat or fish spread
L is the abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A spread covers a big serving dish.
explanation.definitionFit: A plate is a flat dish for serving or eating food.

clue.text: The opposite of stern heads of schools taking extreme measures

indicators.note: the heads of words are their opening letters, so only those are kept

parts.note: first letters of the four words

explanation.surface: Schools, far from being stern, are resorting to drastic action.
explanation.walkthrough: Stern sounds like strict, but it is the back of a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: On a boat the stem is the front of the bow, the end opposite the stern.

clue.text: One who might help when out of one's depth?

definitions.text: One who might help when out of one's depth?

parts.words: One who might help when out of one's depth?
parts.note: surface reading: a mentor who supports someone overwhelmed by a task
setter's reading: literally in water too deep to stand in

explanation.surface: A helper for someone struggling beyond their abilities.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom for being overwhelmed is taken literally, about swimming.
explanation.definitionFit: A lifeguard rescues swimmers in difficulty in deep water.

clue.text: Mug? The compiler had nothing to fill it

parts.note: the setter saying 'I had', contracted

indicators.note: something that fills another sits inside it

parts.note: taken as written
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: The setter had nothing to put in a mug.
explanation.definitionFit: A mug is British slang for a gullible fool, an idiot.

clue.text: A pain in the neck for Mr Astley?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a sprain or crick, especially in the neck
second meaning: the first name of singer Astley

explanation.walkthrough: Rick Astley is the 1980s singer of 'Never Gonna Give You Up', whose song became the 'rickrolling' prank, a pain in the neck in its own way.
explanation.definitionFit: A rick is a muscle strain such as a cricked neck, and it is also Astley's first name.

clue.text: Official under me bungled democratic process

parts.note: a ref is a referee, a match official

indicators.note: bungled work is messed up, so these letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A subordinate official made a mess of a vote.
explanation.definitionFit: A referendum is a direct popular vote on a single question, a democratic procedure.
